subtopic: Duty to cooperate with the Board
stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives a Board request to appear and to produce dispensing records connected to a complaint. He is confident the complaint is baseless and simply does not respond. The Board later dismisses the underlying complaint. What is his exposure?

choices.text: No exposure, because dismissal of the underlying complaint resolves the matter.
No exposure, provided he can show the records would not have changed the outcome.
Exposure only if the Board issues a subpoena that he then ignores.
Exposure only if the underlying complaint had ultimately been substantiated.
Exposure, because failing without cause to cooperate is itself a ground for discipline.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 10.03(1)(q) makes it an independent ground for discipline to fail, without cause, to cooperate with any Board request to appear or to provide requested information, to fail to respond to a Board subpoena, or to fail to furnish records, documents, information or testimony to which the Board is legally entitled. The ground stands on its own and does not depend on the outcome of the underlying complaint.

choice_analysis.A: Dismissal of the complaint does not dispose of the separate non-cooperation ground.
choice_analysis.B: The materiality of the records is not the test.
choice_analysis.C: The ground covers requests as well as subpoenas.
choice_analysis.D: The ground does not depend on the underlying complaint being substantiated.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: non-cooperation without cause is a standalone ground.

related_facts: The duty extends to records, documents, information and testimony to which the Board is legally entitled.
explanation.mpje_trap: Winning on the underlying complaint does not cure a separate failure to cooperate with the investigation.

reasoning_steps: Separate the underlying complaint from the duty to cooperate
Note that the ground covers requests to appear and to provide information
Apply the ground independently of the complaint's disposition
